title: "SVM"
output: html_document

# Load data
```{r}
library(kernlab)
library(caret)

madness_train <- readRDS("training_data.rds")
madness_test <- readRDS("testing_data.rds")

# ksvm only does classification if the outcome is a factor
madness_train$winner <- as.factor(madness_train$winner)
madness_test$winner <- as.factor(madness_test$winner)
```

## Step 2: Training a model on the data (linear kernel)
```{r}
# begin by training a simple SVM with a linear kernel ("vanilladot")
madness_classifier <- ksvm(winner ~ ., data = madness_train,
                           kernel = "vanilladot", prob.model = TRUE)

madness_classifier
```

## Step 3: Evaluating model performance (linear kernel)
```{r}
# probability that team 1 wins
madness_predictions <- predict(madness_classifier, madness_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]

head(madness_predictions)

svm_confusion <- confusionMatrix(
  factor(ifelse(madness_predictions > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
  as.factor(madness_test$winner),
  positive = "1"
)
svm_confusion
```

## Step 4: Testing other kernels

We now test two other kernels to see whether a non-linear boundary changes performance.

### RBF kernel
```{r}
madness_classifier_rbf <- ksvm(winner ~ ., data = madness_train,
                               kernel = "rbfdot", prob.model = TRUE)

madness_predictions_rbf <- predict(madness_classifier_rbf, madness_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]

svm_rbf_confusion <- confusionMatrix(
  factor(ifelse(madness_predictions_rbf > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
  as.factor(madness_test$winner),
  positive = "1"
)
svm_rbf_confusion
```

### Polynomial kernel
```{r}
madness_classifier_poly <- ksvm(winner ~ ., data = madness_train,
                                kernel = "polydot",
                                kpar = list(degree = 2), prob.model = TRUE)

madness_predictions_poly <- predict(madness_classifier_poly, madness_test, type = "probabilities")[, "1"]

svm_poly_confusion <- confusionMatrix(
  factor(ifelse(madness_predictions_poly > 0.5, 1, 0), levels = c(0, 1)),
  as.factor(madness_test$winner),
  positive = "1"
)
svm_poly_confusion
```

## Compare kernels
```{r}
kernel_comparison <- data.frame(
  Kernel = c("Linear (vanilladot)", "RBF (rbfdot)", "Polynomial, degree 2 (polydot)"),
  Accuracy = c(svm_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
               svm_rbf_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
               svm_poly_confusion$overall["Accuracy"]),
  Sensitivity = c(svm_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                  svm_rbf_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                  svm_poly_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
  Specificity = c(svm_confusion$byClass["Specificity"],
                  svm_rbf_confusion$byClass["Specificity"],
                  svm_poly_confusion$byClass["Specificity"])
)

# clean up the row names (otherwise they show as "Accuracy", "Accuracy1", ...)
row.names(kernel_comparison) <- NULL

kernel_comparison
```
